answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a mutual bond: a newcomer must lock a small deposit co-signed by two long-lived peers, like a vine that only grows when rooted in existing trust. If the newcomer duplicates work or floods the market, the bond is slashed and the vouchers lose stake too, so the tide of cheap fake identities meets a rising cost. Each extra identity funded from the same source pays a steeper bond, turning the attacker's profit spiral into a loss spiral while honest single agents pay almost nothing.
